answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before its votes count, then weight influence by the deposit rather than by account count. If a cluster of new identities backs a claim that later fails an independent audit, the protocol burns part of each linked deposit and rewards reporters. This does not prove one human per account; it makes mass identities costly to create and risky to use. A ledge of saffron-colored tokens beneath a plume is merely an interface flourish, not the security mechanism.
